question.problem: A car travels at a speed of $2.5$ kilometers per minute. What is this in kilometers per hour?
question.worked_solution:
We are given the units $\frac{\text{km}}{\text{min}},$ and we want to convert this into $\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}.$ To figure out what we need to multiply by, we can set up an equation to help us:

$$
\frac{\text{km}}{\text{min}}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}
$$

We want to replace $\text{min}$ with $\text{hour}.$ To get rid of $\text{min},$ we can put $\text{min}$ in the numerator so that it cancels out. To introduce $\text{hour},$ we can put $\text{hour}$ in the denominator.

$$
\frac{\text{km}}{\cancel{\text{min}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{min}}}{\text{hour}}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}
$$

So, our conversion formula is

$$
\frac{\text{km}}{\text{min}}\cdot \frac{\text{min}}{\text{hour}}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}.
$$

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

- The rate given in the problem statement is $2.5\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{min}}.$

- There are $60$ minutes in one hour.

Applying our conversion formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2.5\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{min}} & =2.5\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{min}}\cdot 60\,\frac{\text{min}}{\text{hour}} \\  & =2.5\cdot 60(\frac{\text{km}}{\cancel{\text{min}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{min}}}{\text{hour}}) \\  & =150\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}.\end{aligned}
$$
